title: Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

reading.body:
This is a case of a deployed tool carrying hidden behaviour that its users could not see. The markers were embedded in the system prompt of a released version of Claude Code, and they changed the tool's output only when the environment pointed at certain base URLs, timezones, or hostnames. The mechanism was conditional, so it stayed invisible to anyone running the tool against the official endpoint.

The failure sits in the gap between what a tool does and what its users are told it does. Detection would have required inspecting the shipped prompt and decoding the embedded strings, which is what the developer who reported it did. Ordinary use of the tool would never surface the behaviour, and the reporting states the bypass is trivial.

The reporting describes the keyword and domain lists as aimed at Chinese AI labs, proxy gateways, and resellers, and one outlet reports Anthropic called the tracker an experiment. It is not established that the markers were used to collect data, to block anyone, or for any purpose beyond what the reporting attributes to Anthropic's own statement.

reports.title: Claude Code Is Steganographically Marking Requests
Anthropic is removing its covert code for catching Chinese competitors
Claude Code’s hidden tracker was an “experiment,” says Anthropic
Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

summary:
A developer inspecting Claude Code version 2.1.196 found hidden markers in the system prompt. The tool silently alters the date string based on the API base URL and timezone. If the timezone is Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi, the date separator changes from a hyphen to a slash. If the hostname matches a known domain or AI lab keyword, the apostrophe in the date sentence changes to a different Unicode character. The domain and keyword lists are stored as base64 strings and decoded with an XOR key.

The trigger is the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL environment variable. The decoded keyword list includes deepseek, moonshot, minimax, zhipu, and others, while the domain list covers Chinese tech firms and many proxy or reseller gateways. The author suggests Anthropic may use this to detect resellers and distillation pipelines. For most users with the official endpoint or no base URL override, nothing changes. The article notes the bypass is trivial and no next steps are stated.
